_note: AI-drafted Call to Worship — pending Wilson's curation.

registers.label: Spare
lines: The heavens are telling the glory of God.
Day to day pours forth speech.
God speaks the commandments on the mountain.
Your words, O Lord, are sweeter than honey.
Jesus drives the sellers from his Father's house.
Zeal for your house consumes him.
The cross looks like folly, but it is the power of God.
Come, let us worship the crucified Lord. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: The skies tell it without a word, and on the mountain God carves it in stone: here is the way to live.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross.
In the temple courts, Jesus overturns the tables, clearing a path back to his Father.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross.
Tear down this temple, he says, and in three days I will raise it, and we are still learning what he meant.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross.
To the world the cross is foolishness; to us who are being saved, it is the power of God.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross.
So come into the house made clean, and worship.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross. Amen.

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: The heavens tell it; the stone tablets spell it.
Lead us in your way.
Jesus clears the temple of all that sells.
Lead us in your way.
Foolishness to the world, the cross is God's power.
Lead us in your way.
Come into the house made clean, and worship.
Lead us in your way. Amen.
